item.title: GE Roundabout, Bishop’s Cleeve – lane markings/signage approaching from A435 Evesham Bypass, 18th September
item.description:
I would like to raise a question regarding the lane guidance at the GE Roundabout at Bishop’s Cleeve. When approaching the roundabout from the A435 Evesham Bypass, heading towards Cheltenham, the road alignment makes the route towards Cheltenham feel somewhat ambiguous. From a driver’s perspective, the movement towards Cheltenham appears to be effectively straight ahead, albeit following the curve of the road. However, because of the physical shape of the approach and the way the lanes appear to lead into the roundabout, many drivers seem to naturally use the right-hand lane, as this feels like the appropriate lane for the direction they are travelling. This raises a question about what lane drivers are actually intended to use for the Cheltenham exit. I would be grateful if you could clarify: 1. Which lane is intended for traffic approaching from the A435 Evesham Bypass and travelling towards Cheltenham? 2. Is the Cheltenham exit considered a straight-ahead movement or a right-turn movement for lane-positioning purposes? 3. If there is an intended lane, could clearer lane arrows or road markings be considered? I ask particularly because this is an area used regularly by learner drivers, and I feel the current road layout could potentially lead to uncertainty or inconsistent lane choice. The council has recently carried out improvement works around the GE Roundabout, including changes to pedestrian and cycle crossings. However, the published information states that the number of vehicle lanes and vehicle movements at the roundabout were not changed. It would therefore be useful to know whether clearer lane guidance could be considered as part of any future works or road-marking review. Thank you.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): A435, Bishop's Cleeve, Tewkesbury
Report on FixMyStreet
